Fact.Name: Part II row: tax withheld on a dividend that failed the section 901(k) holding period
Fact.Description:
How much of the tax entered in columns (q) through (t) for this country was withheld on a dividend for which the section 901(k) holding period was NOT met: the stock was not held for at least 16 days within the 31-day period beginning 15 days before the ex-dividend date, or, for preference dividends attributable to periods aggregating more than 366 days, not held for at least 46 days within the 91-day period (IRC 901(k)(3) substitutes 45 days and a 91-day period). Section 901(k) denies the credit for that tax outright, so it is subtracted from column (u) and never reaches Form 1116 line 8. AN INTAKE LEAF: no fact in this dictionary pairs a dividend with its ex-dividend date or with a holding period, so the disqualified share is a quantity only the filer holds. UNANSWERED SUBTRACTS NOTHING, so every return that does not state one computes column (u) exactly as it did before.
HOW TO COUNT THE DAYS, which the publication prints and this question used to leave to the filer: count the day you sold the stock, do not count the day you acquired it, and do not count any day on which you were protected from risk of loss. Pub. 514's own two worked examples are the boundary pair, and they are the node tests this row is pinned with. Example 1: stock bought November 3 and sold November 19, ex-dividend November 5, so the 31-day period began October 21 and the stock was held 16 days, from November 4 until November 19 - the credit is allowed and NOTHING is entered here. Example 2: the same facts with a November 14 sale is 11 days, and the tax on that dividend is entered here and lost. Those examples carry DAYS and no dollars; the dollar figures in the pinned cases are synthetic.
THE SECURITIES-DEALER EXCEPTION IS BUILT, AS A SECOND AMOUNT AND NOT AS A REWORDING OF THIS QUESTION. IRC 901(k)(4) lifts the bar for a qualified tax on a security held in the active conduct of a foreign securities-dealing business, and the relief is taken on the row below (/form1116ColumnUQualifiedSection901kDealerTax), which asks the dealer for the qualifying dollars and subtracts them. THIS QUESTION STAYS FACTUAL ON PURPOSE: re-wording it to ask how much tax section 901(k) DISALLOWS would hand every Form 1116 dividend filer the whole of section 901(k) - the 16/31 test, the 45/91 preference substitution, the section 246(c) counting rules and the dealer triple - and a filer who has never heard of the section would answer $0 in good faith. That trades a taxpayer-safe over-refusal of a near-empty population for a silent over-credit of the whole population. Days held come off a brokerage statement; a legal conclusion does not.
IRC 901(k)(5) imports the holding-period computation rules of section 246(c)(3) and (4), which the counting sentence above states in the publication's own words.
AND THE SIBLING RULE THIS ROW DOES NOT CARRY: IRC 901(l) states the same minimum holding period for withholding tax on income and gain OTHER than dividends, and this writable asks only about dividends because the printed instruction item 5 it quotes does. It is asked on this row as its own amount, /form1116ForeignCountries/*/writableColumnUTaxesOnNonDividendIncomeFailingSection901lHoldingPeriod.

Because column (viii) is only the page 1 subtotal of the same line, adding columns (viii) through (xiii) is the same arithmetic as summing line 5 over all eleven carryover years, so this is a guarded sum over the whole /form1116CarryoverYears collection rather than an add of the seven printed cells. No dictionary fact reads this print value even so.
